transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-10-12 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood, AE); Samira Khan (Redwood, SE); Maya Reynolds (Sycamore, CTO); Ethan Wu (Sycamore, Head of Infra); Leila Torres (Sycamore, Procurement)

Summary:
Quick renewal/expansion check-in: Sycamore wants to move from a 12-month committed plan to a 24-month with an EU edge region add-on and a modest capacity bump during Q4 peak. Discussed throughput targets, options for dedicated vs hosted with reserved burst, security/KMS questions, and next steps to run benchmarks and finalize contract amendment.

Topics:
- Current usage and projected Q4 peak
- EU edge region onboarding and data residency questions
- Pricing on 24-month commitment + burst pool for Black Friday window
- Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
- Pilot/benchmark plan and timelines

Action items (see metadata list above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Park: alright good afternoon everyone, thanks for carving out time. i'm jordan from redwood, will kick us off — quick agenda: project status, capacity ask, eu edge, security follow-ups, then next steps. sound good?
[00:18] Maya Reynolds: yep yep thanks jordan, we just want to make sure we don't hit throttles during our shopping surge. we saw a couple spikes last year and want to avoid that.
[00:28] Ethan Wu: yeah hi all, ethan here. last holiday season we spiked to about 3.2k concurrent requests for recommendations, latency slipped a bit at the 95/99 percentiles. goal is to cap 99th at 200ms for typical gen calls, with a soft target of 120ms for sessionized flows.
[00:48] Samira Khan: okay good detail, that helps. are those gen calls with long context? what's token length distribution?
[00:56] Ethan Wu: mostly short prompts, mean length 60-80 tokens, but we have about 10% of sessions that hit 400-800 tokens when users do deep review.
[01:10] Jordan Park: perfect. on the redwood side, for your current plan you're on a 12-month reserved baseline — we have capacity headroom but for guaranteed throughput during the surge we'd recommend either a temporary burst pool or moving to a higher reserved tier. both are possible with a 24-month commit which unlocks better unit pricing.
[01:32] Leila Torres: pricing is the crux — procurement wants predictability and a simpler amendment rather than renegotiating the whole contract. can you outline high-level delta?
[01:42] Jordan Park: yes — high-level: 24-month committed baseline about +30% capacity, lower per-token and per-embedding rates, add EU edge region as a billable add-on (flat monthly for the edge plus usage). burst pool available as a short-term add-on charged by peak capacity hours. i'll send exact numbers after this call.
[02:05] Maya Reynolds: on the EU edge, we need data residency for EU customers and separate audit logs. can Redwood replicate logs to our SIEM in eu-west and keep key material region-scoped?
[02:17] Samira Khan: short answer: yes we support region-scoped KMS integration, and logs can be forwarded to your SIEM — we'll need the syslog/endpoints and an architecture freeze to get ip allowlists. samira typing notes...
[02:33] Ethan Wu: ok that's important — also around private deployments: we're evaluating private dedicated because of regulatory stuff, but for now edge region plus VPC peering might be enough. what's the rollout complexity?
[02:44] Samira Khan: for EU edge it's a control plane in our hosted offering with compute nodes located in eu-west. onboarding is largely config-driven: vpc peering, routes, ip allowlist, and KMS keys in your region. for private on-prem we'd need longer lead times (hardware, install).
[03:04] Jordan Park: to be explicit: we can do hosted + EU edge within ~4-6 weeks if you approve the amendment and provide network contacts, shorter if you accept a canary with limited traffic first. private on-prem tends to be multiple months.
[03:20] Leila Torres: procurement will need the security packet — SOC2 Type II report, encryption at rest docs, and a sample amendment. can you push those?
[03:28] Jordan Park: absolutely, i'll attach SOC2, encryption writeup, and a draft amendment. also default SLA language and availability targets.
[03:35] Maya Reynolds: great. another question — will adding the EU region change model variants available? we use a quantized variant for cost efficiency.
[03:43] Samira Khan: model availability is consistent; however some quantized builds have different performance on certain hardware. we'll surface recommended quantization/profile for eu nodes in the benchmark. we can also route traffic to the nearest compatible instance if needed.
[03:59] Ethan Wu: routing fallback is good — we don't want failed requests if eu capacity is constrained. do you support automated fallback to another region with reduced latency?
[04:09] Samira Khan: yes, smart routing policy can fail over to a compatible model variant in another region with a controlled latency/cost policy. we'll show you routing policy config examples.
[04:20] Jordan Park: quick aside, any competitors in your selection process?
[04:24] Maya Reynolds: we've done some benchmarking with Anthropic and a little bit with OpenAI for baseline. also internal tests on SageMaker for private hosts. leaning toward redwood because of lower tail latency and the dev experience.
[04:38] Samira Khan: thanks for the context. on benchmarks — we'd like a reference run: 2-4 hour soak with your synthetic traffic and a peak window simulating 3.5k concurrency. we'll need a sample dataset and an ip whitelist.
[04:52] Ethan Wu: we can provide a replay file and traffic curve. is there a cost to run the benchmark?
[04:58] Jordan Park: no charge for the benchmark if it's tied to a committed amendment; for purely exploratory runs there's a small usage fee. in the amendment scenario we'll include a benchmark window.
[05:10] Leila Torres: procurement question — if we move to 24 months and we overshoot usage, how are overages handled? we need clear buckets.
[05:19] Jordan Park: typically baseline committed capacity covers X tokens/second and hours; overage billed at discounted usage rate, burst pool covers transient peaks and is billed by peak hour or hourly reserved increments. we can add a soft cap alerting before billing.
[05:36] Maya Reynolds: can we get an example invoice line item? helps finance sign off.
[05:41] Jordan Park: yes, i'll include sample invoice lines in the amendment doc.
[05:46] Samira Khan: technical note: for your 400-800 token tails we recommend increasing KV cache memory on the instance type and bumping batch window slightly for those sessions to keep per-token latency stable. we'll propose precise kernel/instance combos in the benchmark plan.
[06:02] Ethan Wu: perfect. latency at 99th is most important to product. our execs care about that more than raw throughput.
[06:09] Jordan Park: understood. we'll include 99th-latency-driven configs in the runbook.
[06:15] Maya Reynolds: timeline-wise, we want the amendment signed by Oct 31 to be in place before Black Friday prep — is that realistic?
[06:23] Jordan Park: yes if we move quickly: i'll send the draft amendment and security pack by Oct 15; you sign, signoff on network, and we'll schedule benchmarks week of Oct 25; if benchmark looks good we flip the edge on for the peak.
[06:37] Leila Torres: procurement needs contract language for auto-renewal and termination clauses — last time those tripped up our legal team.
[06:45] Jordan Park: we'll mark the amendment to explicitly call out term length (24 months), renewal behavior (explicit renewal unless opt-out 60 days prior), and termination rights. i'll propose language to be attorney-reviewed.
[06:57] Samira Khan: i'm going to call out one risk: quantized model performance variance across CPUs/GPUs; we'll include a fallback model and a regression test in the benchmark to catch quality drift.
[07:09] Ethan Wu: good. also, SSO and RBAC — we need SAML SSO and fine-grain roles for dev vs ops.
[07:16] Samira Khan: supported — SAML + SCIM provisioning, role-based access controls for routes and billing views. we'll include a plan for SCIM setup during onboarding.
[07:27] Maya Reynolds: final question before we wrap: can you guarantee no egress of EU customer PII outside the EU region? legal will ask.
[07:36] Jordan Park: we will commit to regional data residency for request/response logs for EU-scoped customers; we'll include that in the amendment as an obligation and detail the export-only circumstances (e.g., customer-driven cross-region replication) and opt-in.
[07:52] Leila Torres: ok good. next steps recap?
[07:55] Jordan Park: sure — i'll send amendment + SOC2 + network diagrams + sample invoice lines by Oct 15. samira will share benchmark plan by Oct 22. ethan will provide traffic replay and SLOs by Oct 18. leila will share procurement timing and PO process by Oct 20. then we aim to run the benchmark week of Oct 25 and target sign-off by Oct 31.
[08:18] Maya Reynolds: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[08:21] Jordan Park: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and I will drop calendar invites for the benchmark kickoff.
[08:28] (meeting end)

Notes on transcription: there are a few mis-heard words around technical acronyms, e.g., 'kv cache' was sometimes transcribed as 'k v cash' and 'SCIM' as 'skim'. speaker labels are mostly correct but may show generic tags in some exports.
